mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST (new single-family houses started) and INDPRO over the past six months indicates synchronized growth in housing and manufacturing demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the 6-month correlation between HOUST and INDPRO exceeds 0.7.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months of >0.5% monthly PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals that households are drawing down savings to finance consumption, which temporarily supports demand but ultimately increases debt risk and may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
